| <code>voiceEnabled</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether the phone numbers can receive calls. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>excludeAllAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require an [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>excludeLocalAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a local [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>excludeForeignAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a foreign [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>beta</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to read phone numbers that are new to the Twilio platform. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `true`. |
| <code>nearNumber</code> | <code>string?</code> | Given a phone number, find a geographically close number within `distance` miles. Distance defaults to 25 miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>nearLatLong</code> | <code>string?</code> | Given a latitude/longitude pair `lat,long` find geographically close numbers within `distance` miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>distance</code> | <code>int?</code> | The search radius, in miles, for a `near_` query.  Can be up to `500` and the default is `25`. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inPostalCode</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a particular postal code. Given a phone number, search within the same postal code as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inRegion</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a particular region, state, or province. Given a phone number, search within the same region as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inRateCenter</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a specific rate center, or given a phone number search within the same rate center as that number. Requires `in_lata` to be set as well. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inLata</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a specific local access and transport area ([LATA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_access_and_transport_area)). Given a phone number, search within the same [LATA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_access_and_transport_area) as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inLocality</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a particular locality or city. Given a phone number, search within the same Locality as that number. |
| <code>faxEnabled</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether the phone numbers can receive faxes. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>pageSize</code> | <code>long?</code> | How many resources to return in each list page. The default is 50, and the maximum is 1000. |

| <code>contains</code> | <code>string?</code> | Matching pattern to identify phone numbers. This pattern can be between 2 and 16 characters long and allows all digits (0-9) and all non-diacritic latin alphabet letters (a-z, A-Z). It accepts four meta-characters: `*`, `%`, `+`, `$`. The `*` and `%` meta-characters can appear multiple times in the pattern. To match wildcards at the beginning or end of the pattern, use `*` to match any single character or `%` to match a sequence of characters. If you use the wildcard patterns, it must include at least two non-meta-characters, and wildcards cannot be used between non-meta-characters. To match the beginning of a pattern, start the pattern with `+`. To match the end of the pattern, append the pattern with `$`. These meta-characters can't be adjacent to each other. |
| <code>smsEnabled</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether the phone numbers can receive text messages. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>mmsEnabled</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether the phone numbers can receive MMS messages. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>voiceEnabled</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether the phone numbers can receive calls. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>excludeAllAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require an [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>excludeLocalAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a local [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>excludeForeignAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a foreign [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>beta</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to read phone numbers that are new to the Twilio platform. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `true`. |
| <code>nearNumber</code> | <code>string?</code> | Given a phone number, find a geographically close number within `distance` miles. Distance defaults to 25 miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>nearLatLong</code> | <code>string?</code> | Given a latitude/longitude pair `lat,long` find geographically close numbers within `distance` miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>distance</code> | <code>int?</code> | The search radius, in miles, for a `near_` query.  Can be up to `500` and the default is `25`. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inPostalCode</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a particular postal code. Given a phone number, search within the same postal code as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inRegion</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a particular region, state, or province. Given a phone number, search within the same region as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inRateCenter</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a specific rate center, or given a phone number search within the same rate center as that number. Requires `in_lata` to be set as well. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inLata</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a specific local access and transport area ([LATA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_access_and_transport_area)). | <code>contains</code> | <code>string?</code> | Matching pattern to identify phone numbers. This pattern can be between 2 and 16 characters long and allows all digits (0-9) and all non-diacritic latin alphabet letters (a-z, A-Z). It accepts four meta-characters: `*`, `%`, `+`, `$`. The `*` and `%` meta-characters can appear multiple times in the pattern. To match wildcards at the beginning or end of the pattern, use `*` to match any single character or `%` to match a sequence of characters. If you use the wildcard patterns, it must include at least two non-meta-characters, and wildcards cannot be used between non-meta-characters. To match the beginning of a pattern, start the pattern with `+`. To match the end of the pattern, append the pattern with `$`. These meta-characters can't be adjacent to each other. |

| <code>mmsEnabled</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether the phone numbers can receive MMS messages. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>voiceEnabled</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether the phone numbers can receive calls. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>excludeAllAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require an [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>excludeLocalAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a local [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>excludeForeignAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a foreign [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>beta</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to read phone numbers that are new to the Twilio platform. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `true`. |
| <code>nearNumber</code> | <code>string?</code> | Given a phone number, find a geographically close number within `distance` miles. Distance defaults to 25 miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>nearLatLong</code> | <code>string?</code> | Given a latitude/longitude pair `lat,long` find geographically close numbers within `distance` miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>distance</code> | <code>int?</code> | The search radius, in miles, for a `near_` query.  Can be up to `500` and the default is `25`. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inPostalCode</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a particular postal code. Given a phone number, search within the same postal code as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inRegion</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a particular region, state, or province. Given a phone number, search within the same region as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inRateCenter</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a specific rate center, or given a phone number search within the same rate center as that number. Requires `in_lata` to be set as well. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inLata</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a specific local access and transport area ([LATA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_access_and_transport_area)). Given a phone number, search within the same [LATA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_access_and_transport_area) as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inLocality</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a particular locality or city. Given a phone number, search within the same Locality as that number. |
| <code>faxEnabled</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether the phone numbers can receive faxes. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>pageSize</code> | <code>long?</code> | How many resources to return in each list page. The default is 50, and the maximum is 1000. |

This pattern can be between 2 and 16 characters long and allows all digits (0-9) and all non-diacritic latin alphabet letters (a-z, A-Z). It accepts four meta-characters: `*`, `%`, `+`, `$`. The `*` and `%` meta-characters can appear multiple times in the pattern. To match wildcards at the beginning or end of the pattern, use `*` to match any single character or `%` to match a sequence of characters. If you use the wildcard patterns, it must include at least two non-meta-characters, and wildcards cannot be used between non-meta-characters. To match the beginning of a pattern, start the pattern with `+`. To match the end of the pattern, append the pattern with `$`. These meta-characters can't be adjacent to each other. |

| <code>voiceEnabled</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether the phone numbers can receive calls. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>excludeAllAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require an [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>excludeLocalAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a local [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>excludeForeignAddressRequired</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a foreign [Address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/api/address). Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`. |
| <code>beta</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to read phone numbers that are new to the Twilio platform. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `true`. |
| <code>nearNumber</code> | <code>string?</code> | Given a phone number, find a geographically close number within `distance` miles. Distance defaults to 25 miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>nearLatLong</code> | <code>string?</code> | Given a latitude/longitude pair `lat,long` find geographically close numbers within `distance` miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>distance</code> | <code>int?</code> | The search radius, in miles, for a `near_` query.  Can be up to `500` and the default is `25`. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |

Given a phone number, search within the same [LATA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_access_and_transport_area) as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada. |
| <code>inLocality</code> | <code>string?</code> | Limit results to a particular locality or city. Given a phone number, search within the same Locality as that number. |

Conversations that were created on or after this date will be included in the results. The date must be in ISO8601 format, specifically starting at the beginning of the specified date (YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z), for precise filtering. This parameter can be combined with other filters. If this filter is used, the returned list is sorted by latest conversation creation date in descending order. |

Only conversations that were created on or before this date will appear in the results.  The date must be in ISO8601 format, specifically capturing up to the end of the specified date (YYYY-MM-DDT23:59:59Z), to ensure that conversations from the entire end day are included. This parameter can be combined with other filters. If this filter is used, the returned list is sorted by latest conversation creation date in descending order. |

<dd>

The Lookup API allows you to query information on a phone number so that you can make a trusted interaction with your user

</dd>
</dl>

### Usage

<dl>
<dd>

```csharp
try
{
    var response = await client.LookupsV2PhoneNumber.FetchPhoneNumber3(phoneNumber,
        fields,
        countryCode,
        firstName,
        lastName,
        addressLine1,
        addressLine2,
        city,
        state,
        postalCode,
        addressCountryCode,
        nationalId,
        dateOfBirth,
        lastVerifiedDate,
        verificationSid,
        partnerSubId);
    // TODO: Handle 'response' of type LookupResponse
}
catch (SdkException<RawError> ex)
{
    // TODO: Handle 'ex.Error' of type RawError
}
```

</dd>
</dl>

### Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>phoneNumber</code> | <code>string</code> | The phone number to lookup in E.164 or national format. Default country code is +1 (North America). |
| <code>fields</code> | <code>string?</code> | A comma-separated list of fields to return. Possible values are validation, caller_name, sim_swap, call_forwarding, line_status, line_type_intelligence, identity_match, reassigned_number, sms_pumping_risk, phone_number_quality_score, pre_fill. |
| <code>countryCode</code> | <code>string?</code> | The [country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) used if the phone number provided is in national format. |
| <code>firstName</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s first name. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>lastName</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s last name. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>addressLine1</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s first address line. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>addressLine2</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s second address line. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>city</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s city. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>state</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s country subdivision, such as state, province, or locality. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>postalCode</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s postal zip code. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>addressCountryCode</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s country, up to two characters. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>nationalId</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s national ID, such as SSN or Passport ID. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>dateOfBirth</code> | <code>string?</code> | User’s date of birth, in YYYYMMDD format. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>lastVerifiedDate</code> | <code>string?</code> | The date you obtained consent to call or text the end-user of the phone number or a date on which you are reasonably certain that the end-user could still be reached at that number. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for reassigned_number package requests. |
| <code>verificationSid</code> | <code>string?</code> | The unique identifier associated with a verification process through verify API. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for pre_fill package requests. |
| <code>partnerSubId</code> | <code>string?</code> | The optional partnerSubId parameter to provide context for your sub-accounts, tenantIDs, sender IDs or other segmentation, enhancing the accuracy of the risk analysis. |

</dd>

| <code>workflowSid</code> | <code>string?</code> | The SID of the Workflow with the Tasks to read. Returns the Tasks controlled by the Workflow identified by this SID. |
| <code>workflowName</code> | <code>string?</code> | The friendly name of the Workflow with the Tasks to read. Returns the Tasks controlled by the Workflow identified by this friendly name. |
| <code>taskQueueSid</code> | <code>string?</code> | The SID of the TaskQueue with the Tasks to read. Returns the Tasks waiting in the TaskQueue identified by this SID. |
| <code>taskQueueName</code> | <code>string?</code> | The `friendly_name` of the TaskQueue with the Tasks to read. Returns the Tasks waiting in the TaskQueue identified by this friendly name. |
| <code>evaluateTaskAttributes</code> | <code>string?</code> | The attributes of the Tasks to read. Returns the Tasks that match the attributes specified in this parameter. |
| <code>routingTarget</code> | <code>string?</code> | A SID of a Worker, Queue, or Workflow to route a Task to |
| <code>ordering</code> | <code>string?</code> | How to order the returned Task resources. By default, Tasks are sorted by ascending DateCreated. This value is specified as: `Attribute:Order`, where `Attribute` can be either `DateCreated`, `Priority`, or `VirtualStartTime` and `Order` can be either `asc` or `desc`. For example, `Priority:desc` returns Tasks ordered in descending order of their Priority. Pairings of sort orders can be specified in a comma-separated list such as `Priority:desc,DateCreated:asc`, which returns the Tasks in descending Priority order and ascending DateCreated Order. The only ordering pairing not allowed is DateCreated and VirtualStartTime. |
| <code>hasAddons</code> | <code>bool?</code> | Whether to read Tasks with Add-ons. If `true`, returns only Tasks with Add-ons. If `false`, returns only Tasks without Add-ons. |

### Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>workspaceSid</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the Workspace with the resource to fetch. |
| <code>workflowSid</code> | <code>string</code> | Returns the list of Tasks that are being controlled by the Workflow with the specified Sid value. |
| <code>endDate</code> | <code>DateTimeOffset?</code> | Only include usage that occurred on or before this date, specified in GMT as an [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date-time. |
| <code>minutes</code> | <code>int?</code> | Only calculate statistics since this many minutes in the past. The default 15 minutes. This is helpful for displaying statistics for the last 15 minutes, 240 minutes (4 hours), and 480 minutes (8 hours) to see trends. |
| <code>startDate</code> | <code>DateTimeOffset?</code> | Only calculate statistics from this date and time and later, specified in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. |
| <code>taskChannel</code> | <code>string?</code> | Only calculate cumulative statistics on this TaskChannel. Can be the TaskChannel's SID or its `unique_name`, such as `voice`, `sms`, or `default`. |
| <code>splitByWaitTime</code> | <code>string?</code> | A comma separated list of values that describes the thresholds, in seconds, to calculate statistics on. For each threshold specified, the number of Tasks canceled and reservations accepted above and below the specified thresholds in seconds are computed. For example, `5,30` would show splits of Tasks that were canceled or accepted before and after 5 seconds and before and after 30 seconds. This can be used to show short abandoned Tasks or Tasks that failed to meet an SLA. TaskRouter will calculate statistics on up to 10,000 Tasks for any given threshold. |

</dd>
</dl>

}

### Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>workspaceSid</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the Workspace to fetch. |
| <code>endDate</code> | <code>DateTimeOffset?</code> | Only include usage that occurred on or before this date, specified in GMT as an [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date-time. |
| <code>minutes</code> | <code>int?</code> | Only calculate statistics since this many minutes in the past. The default 15 minutes. This is helpful for displaying statistics for the last 15 minutes, 240 minutes (4 hours), and 480 minutes (8 hours) to see trends. |
| <code>startDate</code> | <code>DateTimeOffset?</code> | Only calculate statistics from this date and time and later, specified in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. |
| <code>taskChannel</code> | <code>string?</code> | Only calculate cumulative statistics on this TaskChannel. Can be the TaskChannel's SID or its `unique_name`, such as `voice`, `sms`, or `default`. |
| <code>splitByWaitTime</code> | <code>string?</code> | A comma separated list of values that describes the thresholds, in seconds, to calculate statistics on. For each threshold specified, the number of Tasks canceled and reservations accepted above and below the specified thresholds in seconds are computed. For example, `5,30` would show splits of Tasks that were canceled or accepted before and after 5 seconds and before and after 30 seconds. This can be used to show short abandoned Tasks or Tasks that failed to meet an SLA. TaskRouter will calculate statistics on up to 10,000 Tasks for any given threshold. |

</dd>
</dl>

<dd>

**OnSuccess**: <code>[TaskrouterV1WorkspaceWorkspaceCumulativeStatistics](Models/TaskrouterV1WorkspaceWorkspaceCumulativeStatistics.cs)</code>
